LISTENER’S

GUIDE

Thank you for purchasing Michael Lewis’ The Big Short.

This exclusive Listener’s Guide gives you an overview of the complex economic terms used throughout the book.

GLOSSARY OF (BIG, SCARY) ECONOMIC TERMS

Collateralized debt obligation (CDO):

A bunch of loans bundled together and sold off to investors. As the borrowers pay back the loans, the investors get the money.

CDOs are structured so that investors can choose how much risk to take. The riskier parts of CDOs pay more interest, but take the first losses when borrowers don’t pay back their loans. The safer parts pay less interest, but payments keep flowing longer.

...

More narrowly, to fail to meet the original terms of a loan.

Equities vs. Fixed Income:

Equities are stocks.

Fixed income is bonds.

Hedge:

Kind of like an insurance policy, a hedge is a secondary investment meant to reduce losses if your main investment goes down

Long vs. Short:

If you’re long something, you are betting the price will go up.

If you’re short, you’re betting the price will go down.
